title: The document module is said to own the letter templates and their fields, while Architecture v5 gives templates and merge fields to rwb-comms
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 2 v3 section 7 (DL28); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (tables sheet); Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A1.2 and A2.1
section: A1.2 feature overview FEAT-OCC-01; A2.1 Generate a letter from an approved template; DL28
description: DL28 asks who owns the letter templates and the fields filled into them, and the answer the build uses until decided is 'the document module owns templates and fields; Legal approves wording'. Architecture v5 slide 41 gives rwb-comms notices, templates, merge fields and proof of delivery, slide 17 gives the rwb_comms schema the same four things, and the Ownership Map records template and merge_field as P6 rows. R-PREC puts the Arch v5 catalogue above the Decision Log, so the template and merge-field catalog is this service's, and the DL28 answer is superseded rather than answered here.
evidence: Epic 2 BRD v3 section 7 DL28 ('The document module owns templates and fields; Legal approves wording'). Arch v5 slide 41 (P6 owns notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery) and slide 17 (P6 DB line: schema rwb_comms, notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery). Ownership Map: template and merge_field are P6 rwb_comms. FSD P6 A2.1 and A2.18 field catalog on template.
proposed: Hold the template record, its versions and the Legal approval in rwb-comms, hold the merge-field catalog in rwb-comms, and keep the template body file in rwb-document as a document with a reference on the template row; record DL28 as superseded by D-RCV-60 and close it with the product owner.

title: The signature request is defined as a Communications table while Architecture v5 gives signatures to the document hub
source: Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 (22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5 extract) T3.1 and Appendix T-A; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (tables sheet and rulings sheet)
section: A2.8 Run the e-signature flow; A2.9 Record the signature result; TSD P6 T3.1 signature_request; TSD P6 API-P6-009 to API-P6-011
description: The P6 technical specification defines signature_request as one of its own objects with twelve fields and gives the request and result operations to P6 (API-P6-009, API-P6-010, API-P6-011). Architecture v5 slide 41 gives P5 rwb-document signatures, and slide 16 gives the rwb_document schema signatures. The Ownership Map resolves the split: signature_request is P5 and rwb-comms orchestrates the request through P5's contract. The FSD feature set therefore splits across two services, and neither source states where the request status is read from when the case screen shows it.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T3.1 signature_request (DF-DOC-096 to DF-DOC-107) and T-A.1 API-P6-009 to API-P6-011. Arch v5 slide 41 (P5 owns signatures), slide 16 (P5 DB line). Ownership Map ruling ASM-A6-tables-11: 'signature_request is P5 rwb-document ... P6 orchestrates the request through P5's contract despite TSD P6 v3 defining the table'. FSD P6 A2.8 AC-P6-008-01 and AC-EXC-P6-008-01 to -04.
proposed: This service owns the signature-request operation and the flow: it creates the request through the document hub's contract, applies the signature basis rule, receives the result and calls the treatment service; rwb-document stores the request, its status and the signed copy. Confirm the read path for the request status with P5 before wave 2.

title: Proof of delivery is this service's in Architecture v5 and a read of an ACE view in the functional specification
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17 and 41; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) document control and A2.1 to A2.6; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (tables sheet)
section: A1.1 constraints; A2.2 Dispatch a letter and capture proof of delivery; AC-ALT-P6-001-01
description: Architecture v5 gives rwb-comms proof of delivery as an owned product, and the Ownership Map gives the notice table to P6 with barcode, callback date and delivery status on it. The functional specification, re-based on the ACE database, states that proof of delivery is read from v_ace_pod for a business date, which makes the proof an ACE fact rather than a Workbench fact. Both can hold at once only if the WIN return lands in ACE and this service applies it to the notice, and no source states that path.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 17 (P6 DB line: notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery) and slide 41 (same). FSD P6 document control change note v3 ('proof of delivery reads v_ace_pod') and AC-ALT-P6-001-01 ('v_ace_pod for business date 2026-12-21 returns barcode ...'). TSD P6 T3.1 notice fields DF-LEG-020 to DF-LEG-023 sourced 'WIN'.
owner_role: Solution architect with the ACE team
proposed: Keep the notice record and its proof-of-delivery fields in rwb-comms as the product states, read the proof rows through rwb-source-data's contract, and let this service apply a proof to its notice by barcode; leave the question of which system writes v_ace_pod to the ACE team.

title: Two of the module's business requirements describe the case record view and the case timeline, which the case service owns
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 5.6 and section 11; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) Requirements served
section: Requirements served REQ-OCC-007 and REQ-OCC-008; A2.14 to A2.21 (self-service and history features)
description: REQ-OCC-007 (the case record view shows account, arrears, owner, queue, stage, status, route, timers, contact history, promises, documents and decisions on one screen) and REQ-OCC-008 (a history timeline in order) are written in the Communications module and traced to RWB-SVC-P6 by the Program BRD section 11. Architecture v5 gives the case, its state, queues, tasks and timers to rwb-case, and the case record view is its product; the timeline reads the interaction ledger, which is P1's under the R-PREC default ruling. The Communications contribution is the notice and message block and its history.
evidence: Program BRD v5 section 5.6 REQ-OCC-007 and REQ-OCC-008, and section 11 row 'REQ-OCC-001, REQ-OCC-002, REQ-OCC-007 -> RWB-SVC-P6'. Arch v5 slide 41 (P3 owns case, CMMN state, queues, tasks, allocation, timers) and slide 42 (CaseStateChanged consumer rwb-comms). Program BRD v5 section 10.5 (interaction ledger P1, case timeline and interaction API P3). FSD P6 A2.18 to A2.21.
owner_role: Product owner with the solution architect
proposed: Read both requirements as this service's contribution to the case record view: the notice and message block with its states, and the ordered notice and message history. The view, the timeline and the timer projection stay with rwb-case; the ledger entries stay with rwb-source-data.

title: The message record and its delivery status have no table in the service under Architecture v5
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (tables sheet); Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.3, A2.4, AC-P6-003-01
section: A2.3 Dispatch SMS through NSS; A2.4 Dispatch a LINE message; AC-P6-003-01 and AC-EXC-P6-003-04
description: The functional specification records an SMS or LINE message as an interaction with channel, direction, conduct check result, delivery status and the channel reference (NSS-7781), and shows the failed count on the contact point. Architecture v5 gives rwb-comms three things in its schema (notices, templates, merge fields, with proof of delivery on the notice) and gives the interaction ledger to rwb-source-data under the default ruling. No table in rwb_comms holds a message, so the message record, its delivery status and the channel reference have no stated home.
evidence: FSD P6 AC-P6-003-01 ('an interaction of channel SMS, direction OUTBOUND and conduct check PASSED ... delivery status DELIVERED and reference NSS-7781') and AC-EXC-P6-003-04 ('the contact point has failed count 1'). Arch v5 slide 41 (P6 owns notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery) and slide 17 (schema rwb_comms). Ownership Map: only merge_field, notice and template are P6 tables; ruling ASM-A6-tables-1 keeps the interaction ledger with P1.
proposed: Hold the message outcome as an interaction ledger entry owned by rwb-source-data and read it back through that contract, and add no fourth table to rwb_comms; if the message must be readable inside this service the interaction read path is agreed with P1 before wave 2.

title: The retry limit for a send is five in the functional specification and three in the non-functional requirements
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) AC-EXC-P6-003-03 and AC-EXC-P6-008-03; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 6.4 NFR-026; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13
section: A2.3 exception flows; A2.8 exception flows; NFR-026
description: Two acceptance criteria state that a send is retried until the retry limit of 5 is reached and then placed in the exception queue (NSS and the e-signature path). NFR-026 states three retries per item and then the exception queue, and the Arch v5 retry pattern is 1 minute, 10 minutes, 1 hour and then the dead-letter topic with an alert. One number has to be chosen for the send path.
evidence: FSD P6 AC-EXC-P6-003-03 ('after the retry limit of 5 the send is in the exception queue under rule R-UNI-34'), AC-EXC-P6-004-03, AC-EXC-P6-008-03 ('the retry limit of 5'). Program BRD v5 NFR-026 ('Three retries per item, then the exception queue'). Arch v5 slide 13 (retry 1 min, retry 10 min, retry 1 h, .dlt and alert).
proposed: Use the NFR-026 limit of three retries on the platform schedule and keep the fifth-attempt wording as the source text of the acceptance criteria, with the number confirmed by the solution architect before wave 2.

title: The functional specification names JOB-11 as the retry job for sends, and Architecture v5 makes JOB-11 the outbox relay in every service
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) AC-EXC-P6-003-03 and AC-EXC-P6-008-03; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 and 44; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (jobs sheet)
section: A2.3 exception flows; A2.8 exception flows; JOB-11
description: The functional specification retries a failed SMS or e-signature send through JOB-11 on its schedule. Architecture v5 slide 44 makes JOB-11 the outbox sender in every service (outbox relay to Kafka, every minute), and the Ownership Map gives it to the platform. The retry of an outbound notification is therefore not JOB-11 in v5, and the mechanism that retries it is not named.
evidence: FSD P6 AC-EXC-P6-003-03 ('JOB-11 retries the send on its schedule') and AC-EXC-P6-008-03. Arch v5 slide 44 (JOB-11 Outbox sender, every minute, every service, outbox relay to Kafka) and slide 20 (every service: outbox relay). Ownership Map: JOB-11 owner PLT, no Temporal Schedule (ASM-A6-flows-9, ASM-A6-api-12).
proposed: Read the JOB-11 reference as the platform retry and outbox mechanism, keep JOB-10 as this service's only schedule (WIN notices, 16:00), and name no second job for notification retries.

title: The layout of the WIN registered-mail dispatch file is not stated in any source
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1 to A2.6; Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 (22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5 extract) T5.1 INT-14; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 JOB-10
section: A2.1 Dispatch; A2.2 Dispatch a letter through WIN; INT-14
description: The functional specification fixes what the case and the notice must show after a dispatch (contract reference, barcode, sent date) and the technical specification names INT-14 WIN as a daily file, but no source states the file layout: record set, field list, field order, envelope, naming convention, encoding, or how WIN returns the barcode and the sent date. The field set the notice keeps is stated; the interface definition is not.
evidence: FSD P6 AC-P6-001-01 (WIN acknowledges contract 'CT-88001' with barcode 'RR223344556TH' and sent date 15122026). TSD P6 T5.1 INT-14 (WIN, Out, File, Daily). Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-10 (Airflow file window plus workers) and slide 17 (P6 OUT: Integration deliverFile for WIN letters).
proposed: Take the file layout as a versioned interface definition owned by rwb-integration and hold it as a contract item before wave 2; build the dispatch against a fake of that definition until the real layout is agreed with the WIN owner.

title: No source states the notice, message or proof-of-delivery volumes
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 6.1; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1 metrics; Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 (22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5 extract) T7
section: A2.1 to A2.21 metric tables ('Notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent')
description: The one metric the module states is a quality target (100 percent of notices with proof of delivery). No source gives the number of notices, letters, SMS, LINE messages or returned proofs a month, so no volume test can be sized from the sources. The program's volume table gives only the case count and the document count.
evidence: FSD P6 A2.1 metric table (notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent, monthly). Program BRD v5 section 6.1 NFR-001 (about 23,600 open cases at go-live, 26,500 at the end of 2027; 3,110 new accounts a month) and NFR-004 (about 860,000 documents in 2027, 15 percent inflow growth a year). No notice or message volume appears in the Program BRD, the FSD or the TSD.
owner_role: Business lead with the data lead
proposed: Size the volume test on the document volume of about 860,000 in 2027 as the upper bound for letters and on the interaction volume for messages, and replace both with the measured figures when the business lead provides them.

title: The retention class and period for notices, templates and merge fields are open
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 6.5 NFR-028, NFR-030, NFR-031; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.21; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41
section: NFR-028, NFR-030, NFR-031, NFR-075; A2.21 Apply retention on case closure
description: Every document type must carry a retention class, the decision log has a compliance-set period and case records carry a retention and archive rule, but the periods are open under DL26. The notice record holds the proof of delivery, which a court may ask for after the case closes, so its period cannot follow the case without a decision. No source states the class of a notice, a template version or the merge-field catalog.
evidence: Program BRD v5 NFR-028 ('periods not set'), NFR-030, NFR-031, NFR-072, NFR-074, NFR-075, all open under DL26. FSD P6 A2.21 applies retention on case closure but states no period. Arch v5 slide 41 (P5 owns retention).
proposed: Declare a retention class on the notice record, the template version and the merge-field catalog as versioned data, leave the period to Compliance under DL26, and let rwb-document apply the archive and disposal.

title: The contact repository and the consent state are held in an extension table the source-data service owns
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.18 and A2.5; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (tables sheet); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 5.6 REQ-OCC-010
section: A2.18 Maintain the contact repository; A2.5 conduct check; REQ-OCC-006, REQ-OCC-010
description: The functional specification keeps the verified contact points and the consent state per channel in the Communications repository (contact values from v_ace_contact, consent, verification and failed count in recovery.contact_point_ext). In v5 the four extension tables, contact_point_ext among them, are rwb-source-data's, and the P1 PRD gives contact_point_ext to P1 with the consent and failed-count fields. Consent enforcement stays here, the consent data does not.
evidence: FSD P6 A2.18 description ('consent, verification and failed count are held in recovery.contact_point_ext') and A2.5. Arch v5 slide 41 (P1 owns the extension tables). Ownership Map: contact_point_ext is P1 rwb_source_data. FSD P1 v3 and PRD P1 v1 FR-P1-009 (contact_point_ext: consent, verification, failed count).
proposed: Read the contact point, its consent state and its failed count through rwb-source-data's contract, write a verification and a consent change through that contract, and keep the enforcement (stop, consent refusal, statutory exception) in rwb-comms.

title: It is not stated whether the approval is taken on a template version or on a generated notice
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 5.7 REQ-APD-006; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1 exception flows; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 2 v3 RWB-E2-014
section: A2.1 exception flows AC-EXC-P6-001-02; Arch v5 P6 OUT 'Decision: child: approval'; REQ-APD-006
description: Architecture v5 shows a child approval workflow on the Communications contract; REQ-APD-006 makes demand and recall notices the first use of approval routing, and the Epic 2 story RWB-E2-014 is an approval screen for a generated notice with the case facts and the rule that proposed it. The functional specification also shows Legal approving a template version, and a notice held when the version is withdrawn. Two approvals are therefore in play (the Legal approval of a template version and the approval of a notice) and no source says whether the first is taken through the approval path or recorded on the template row alone.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 17 (P6 OUT: Temporal 'Decision: child: approval'). Program BRD v5 REQ-APD-006 ('Demand and recall notices are approved through this path as the first use of approval routing'). Epic 2 BRD v3 RWB-E2-014 (approval screen showing the generated notice, the case facts and the rule that proposed it). FSD P6 AC-EXC-P6-001-02 (template withdrawn holds the notice) and TSD P6 notice field DF-LEG-032 hold_reason.
proposed: Record the Legal approval on the template version as a decision record written through rwb-decision, and take the notice approval for the demand and recall types through the approval workflow on the generated notice; state both in the story's acceptance criteria.

title: Seven features in the Communications functional specification belong to other services in Architecture v5
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A1.2 and A2.10 to A2.21; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15 to 19 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: A2.10 Match a payment to the plan; A2.11 Raise the plan payment missed event; A2.12 Publish the steering dashboard; A2.13 Give partners identities; A2.19 Custody movement; A2.20 Legal or audit document request; A2.21 Apply retention on case closure
description: The P6 functional specification carries seven features that v5 places elsewhere: payment matching and the plan-payment-missed event (rwb-payment, which publishes PaymentMissed), the steering dashboard (rwb-reporting), partner identities through the external gateway (rwb-partner with rwb-access, on the partner gateway), custody movement, the legal or audit document request and retention on closure (rwb-document). Their IDs and text are kept; none of them is built here.
evidence: Arch v5 slides 15 to 19 and 41 (P8 payment and proceeds matching; P9 measures, snapshots and steering dashboard; S9 panel, partner users and portal; P5 custody, signatures, retention) and slide 42 (PaymentMissed produced by rwb-payment). FSD P6 A1.2 FEAT-OCC-10 to FEAT-OCC-13 and FEAT-COM-06 to FEAT-COM-08.
proposed: Keep the seven features in the source with their identifiers, mark them as not carried in section 5.1 of this PRD with their owning service, and raise the story-level split in the service work packages.

title: Proof of delivery depends on a Section B ACE view that the ACE team has not accepted
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 7 and section 9 DL43; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) document control; PRD P1 v1 section 8.2
section: A2.2 Dispatch a letter and capture proof of delivery; DL43; v_ace_pod
description: The functional specification reads proof of delivery from v_ace_pod, which the P1 read model lists among the 14 Section B views over the RWB-ACE-001 additions (legal and delivery). DL43 is open: the ACE team has not accepted the 14 tables, 12 columns and 80 fields, and the dates are unconfirmed. Proof-of-delivery capture therefore has an unconfirmed dependency, and no fallback path is stated.
evidence: Program BRD v5 section 7 (ACE team dependency, by 21 November 2026 for the 30 November release (tentative)) and section 9 DL43 (open). PRD P1 rwb-source-data v1 section 8.2 (v_ace_lawsuit, v_ace_hearing, v_ace_pod are Section B views). FSD P6 AC-ALT-P6-001-01 to -02.
owner_role: ACE team lead with the solution architect
proposed: Keep proof-of-delivery capture behind its feature flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands and the view is available, and agree the fallback (proof entered by hand against the barcode) with the litigation business owner before wave 2.

title: The notice period timer and the transfer on a non-delivered notice are the case service's, and the trigger is not fixed
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) AC-ALT-P6-001-01 to -02; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 and 42; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (operations sheet)
section: A2.2 alternate flows; NOTICE_PERIOD timer; NOTICE_UNSERVED transfer
description: Two acceptance criteria state effects outside this service: a delivered notice starts a NOTICE_PERIOD timer on the case from the callback date, and an undelivered notice transfers the case to the owner's queue with reason NOTICE_UNSERVED and starts no timer. Architecture v5 gives timers, the case and transfer to rwb-case, and lists NoticeDelivered as consumed by rwb-case; the undelivered path has no event of its own, so the transfer has to be a call. No source states which of the two paths is used.
evidence: FSD P6 AC-ALT-P6-001-01 ('case ... has a running NOTICE_PERIOD timer started on 2026-12-18'), AC-ALT-P6-001-02 ('case ... is transferred to its owner's queue with reason NOTICE_UNSERVED'). Arch v5 slide 41 (P3 owns timers and queues) and slide 42 (NoticeDelivered consumers rwb-litigation, rwb-guarantee, rwb-case). Ownership Map: POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer is P3.
proposed: Publish NoticeDelivered and let rwb-case start the timer from the callback date; for the undelivered path write the decision record here and call rwb-case's transfer operation with reason NOTICE_UNSERVED, and publish NoticeDispatched with the delivery status so reporting sees both.

title: The conduct rule set and the consent rule set have no requirement identifiers in the module's sources
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.5 and A2.6; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 REQ-OCC-005 and REQ-OCC-006; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14
section: A2.5 Run the conduct check; A2.6 Block an outbound contact; VR-P6-005-1 to VR-P6-006-2
description: The module tests every outbound contact against 'the conduct and consent rules' and the Program BRD states the outcome (a conduct check result on every contact, a customer who withdraws consent stops receiving on that channel, statutory notices continue), but no requirement or rule identifier is given for the conduct set, and the rule package that holds it is not named. The only rule identifiers in the module are the validation rules VR-P6-nnn-n and the routing rule references R-LIT-04 and R-LIT-09.
evidence: FSD P6 A2.5 and A2.6 business rules VR-P6-005-1, VR-P6-005-2, VR-P6-006-1, VR-P6-006-2, and BR-P6-005 ('no value a business person may change is written in code'). Program BRD v5 REQ-OCC-005 and REQ-OCC-006. Arch v5 slide 14 (rules governed in rwb-decision, run in the owning service).
owner_role: Conduct and QA officer with rwb-decision
proposed: Take the conduct and consent checks as one versioned rule package governed in rwb-decision and evaluated here, name the package in the story, and let the conduct and QA officer approve its first version.

title: The business requirements document carries no approval for this service and this PRD is issued as Draft
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 2 v3; run rule 9 (D-RCV-60 overlay)
section: Document control and change log; Approval
description: The preconditions of the PRD builder ask for a business requirements document with the status Approved and a Product Owner decision in its governance table. The Program BRD v5 and the Epic 2 BRD v3 are issued as Draft in this run and their approval tables are left empty, so no approval can be recorded for this PRD. The run rules of D-RCV-60 make a missing approval an assumption rather than a stop.
evidence: Program BRD v5 section 12 and its empty approval table; Epic 2 BRD v3 section 10.2 approval table left empty (ASM-B-REQ-BRD-E2-7). Run rules AGENTS.md rule 9 and the D-RCV-60 overlay of this work package.
proposed: Issue this PRD as Draft with an empty approval table and record the missing business approval as an assumption; the Product Owner and the FDA approve the PRD when the business requirements documents are approved.
